title: Trade Marks Amendment (Iconic Symbols of National Identity) Bill 2015
short_title: Trade Marks Amendment (Iconic Symbols of National Identity) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prevent registration of trade marks consisting of signs with national significance or iconic value to Australians and require existing registrations to be revoked.
The Registrar would have to reject qualifying applications and revoke qualifying registered marks, with affected people receiving notice and an opportunity to respond before revocation.
The changes would start the day after Royal Assent and cover applications decided from commencement and marks registered before, at or after that date.
changes: Applications for signs closely resembling protected national or iconic signs could also be rejected.
People aggrieved by a proposed revocation would have an opportunity to be heard.
Revocation decisions under the new rule could be appealed to the Federal Court or Federal Circuit Court.
summary.affected: Trade mark applicants, owners of registered marks, the Registrar and people seeking to use nationally significant or iconic signs would be affected.
